nodes.summary: For identical reporters the covariance is the extrinsic variance: `Cov(X, Y) = Var(E[X | m])`.
nodes.title: Covariance of identical reporters equals extrinsic variance

nodes.summary: The two-reporter extrinsic noise is `Var(E[X | m]) / ⟨X⟩²` (Swain et al. Eq. 8).
nodes.title: Two-reporter formula for extrinsic noise

nodes.summary: Identical reporters have the same mean.
nodes.title: Identical reporters have equal means

nodes.summary: For identical reporters half the mean squared difference is the intrinsic variance: `⟨(X - Y)²⟩ / 2 = ⟨Var(X | m)⟩`.
nodes.title: Half mean squared reporter difference equals intrinsic variance

nodes.summary: The two-reporter intrinsic noise is `⟨Var(X | m)⟩ / ⟨X⟩²` (Swain et al. Eq. 8).
nodes.title: Two-reporter formula for intrinsic noise

nodes.summary: Two reporters of the same gene given the extrinsic σ-algebra `m`: equal conditional means, equal conditional second moments, and conditionally uncorrelated. Conditional independence with identical conditional laws given `m` implies these three conditions.
nodes.title: Identical reporter pair

nodes.summary: Two-reporter decomposition (Swain et al. 2002; Elowitz et al. 2002): for any square-integrable reporters, `η_tot² = η_int² + η_ext²`.
nodes.title: Two-reporter decomposition

nodes.summary: The two-reporter total noise is `Var(X) / ⟨X⟩²`, and it splits into the intrinsic and extrinsic parts by the law of total variance.
nodes.title: Total noise splits into intrinsic and extrinsic parts

conditional.label: conditionally proved

inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
